_doc: How company/tools/model-rank.js ranks models on this company's own work (docs/RANKING.md). Copied to company/work/models/ranking-policy.json at founding; the company's copy is the one read (else this default). Every rule, threshold and weight of the ranking is here, not in code: the scoring is tuned in production. A change bumps version; the ranking records a digest of the policy it used, so a policy change shows as a new ranking even when no work changed. Owner: the people function (the model manager).
_refreshMinutes: how often the dispatcher recomputes the ranking (clamped to 60-1440: at most hourly). Files are rewritten only when the computed body changed.
_windowDays: items closed (DONE) in the last N days are ranked
_oneShotWindowDays: an item is one-shot only if nothing undid it (reopen, revert, fix-forward) within N days of its close
_countUnsettled: false: an item closed less than oneShotWindowDays ago is 'settling' and not scored yet (it would look one-shot only because nothing has had time to undo it)
_minItems: a cell needs at least this many scored items before it may steer anything; below it the cell says 'not enough data'
_interval: the one-shot rate is read as the LOWER bound of this two-sided interval (Wilson score interval), so a small lucky sample does not outrank a large steady one
_score: score = interval lower bound / cost per scored item. cost: 'listUsd' (metered runs at their real usd, subscription runs priced from cost.listPrices), 'usd' (metered usd only: subscription runs cost 0, so do not score on it while any cell is on a subscription) or 'windowTokens' (subscription window share, estimated). per: 'item' or 'change' (cost per accepted change: a PR, else the item itself)
_signals: switch a signal off to leave it out of the ranking entirely (it is then neither shown nor counted)
_oneShot: the signals that make an item not one-shot. Others that may be added: defect, ownerCorrection, premergeFail
_verdicts: a `**Verdict:**` (or `**Review:**`) line in the item's block, or in any handoff block whose `**Item:**` line names the item. Format: `**Verdict:** REVISE by <seat> — check: <the acceptance check run> — <findings>`. requireCheck: a verdict that cites no check (no 'check:') is ignored. A verdict by the item's author (the seat and every seat with a run linked to it) is always ignored
_weights: how much one verdict counts. leadOnOwnReport: a verdict by the seat's department lead, or its manager, on that seat's work (the lead is judged by its reports' results, so its verdicts on them count less)
_defects: competence ledger demerits (company/work/people/competence-events.jsonl) counted as defects against the item whose run (or PR) they trace to, weighted by severity. A row a corroborated ruling voided is left out
_rework: the competence ledger signals that mean the item's change was reverted or needed a fix-forward
_ownerCorrections: an owner correction counts against an item when a ledger row of these signals names one of its runs or its id, or the block carries a `**Owner correction:**` line
_exclude: runs that are not the model's fault are left out, never counted as failures: providerError (the provider failed), sliceCut (a delegated child stopped by the dispatch wall-clock slice). An item whose every run is excluded is not scored. Their cost is reported apart (excludedListUsd)
_cost: how a run's cost is counted: metered runs at the usd the station recorded, subscription runs priced from listPrices, and the subscription window share estimated as its own column

listPrices._doc: USD per 1M tokens, the provider's list price, used only to price SUBSCRIPTION runs (unmetered: the station records usd 0) so cells on a subscription and cells on a metered provider compare on one scale. Matched by the longest key that the run's model starts with (a [..] suffix is ignored). Metered runs use the usd the station recorded. Update when a provider changes its prices.

cost._outputShare: the station records one token count per run (input and output together). This share of the uncached tokens is priced at the output price; 0 prices them all as input (an underestimate on output-heavy work). An assumption to tune
cost._window: subscription window share, reported as its own column until the pacer gives real readings: estimated window tokens = uncached tokens + cachedWeight x cached tokens, for runs of these providers

_tail: tail cost per cell: the cost at this percentile of items, and the mean cost of the most expensive share of items
_graders: a grader whose approval rate differs from the hard one-shot rate of the items it approved or rejected by more than driftPoints (once it has minVerdicts counted verdicts) is flagged
_proposals: a routing proposal is written when a cell with enough data beats a department's current route (company/departments.json routes.<class>) for that class by more than margin (0.15 = 15% higher score). mode shadow: proposals are records only, nothing is applied (applying is a later, owner-switched step). requireRouteData: no proposal while the route's own cell lacks data. allowClaimed: whether a cell whose model the provider did not confirm (no servedModel) may be proposed
_trials: the arm report and decision rule for model trials (docs/RANKING.md §10). Trials themselves are defined in company/work/models/routing-policy.json trials[] (the framework default defines none); a trial's own minItemsPerArm wins over this one. Items are the DONE items whose wakes the dispatcher routed to the trial with the arm applied (route.source trial, applied true); shadow-only items are counted apart, an item worked on two arms counts for none. interval: the one-shot range (Wilson, default: the ranking's confidence). cost: listUsd | usd | windowTokens per accepted item; costStat: mean | median is the figure the rule compares (median, p90 and the hardest share are always shown). Rule: an arm wins when the lower bound of its one-shot range is not below the best other arm's point estimate AND its cost is lower than every other arm's (decision.cheaperThan 'every') or than that best other arm's ('bestOther'), both only once every arm has minItemsPerArm items; otherwise 'no decision yet' with what is missing. stuckDays: the house-ranking duty is due when a running trial has had no routed wake for this many days (or a running or paused trial reached a decision). Delete this section to switch the report off
_tierCapEvaluation: whether executor tier caps pay (docs/RANKING.md §10, the middle-management plan's P3 acceptance), per task class. Capped = scored items whose wake had a tier-cap route applied (route.source tierCap, applied true). baseline 'wouldApply': items whose wake had a tier-cap route recorded but not applied (shadow: the same work, uncapped); 'uncapped': every scored item of the class that no tier-cap route touched. Verdict per class: keep when the estimated claude window tokens per accepted item (cost.window) fell by at least windowCut (0.3 = 30%) AND each rate in rates (revise: share of items with a counted REVISE; reopen: share reopened) is within reworkMaxRatio (1.25x) of the baseline; roll back otherwise; not enough data while either side has fewer than minItems items. dutyWhenModes: the house-ranking duty is due for a roll back while routing-policy.json tierCaps.mode is one of these. Delete this section to switch the evaluation off
_advisorEvaluation: whether a department lead's advice pays (docs/RANKING.md §10, the middle-management plan's P4 bars), per department whose advisor mode is live (company/departments.json): its members' scored items closed since advisor.since against its items closed in as many days before. keep when the consult rate (share of items with a consult) is inside consultRate, the advise runs read at least cachedShareMin of their input from cache (checked once advise runs have token counts), and the cost per accepted item (score.cost) did not rise while the one-shot rate rose at least oneShotGainPoints points OR rework (extra runs + REVISE rounds per item) fell at least reworkCutShare; pause otherwise (the dispatcher pauses the advice once per evaluation when the department's advisor.autoPause.enabled is on; only the owner resumes); not enough data under minItems items on either side or minDays days. A department's advisor.autoPause numbers win over these. Writes company/work/models/advisor-<dept>.md and the advisor part of routing-evaluation.json. Delete this section to switch the report off
_fanoutEvaluation: whether splitting big jobs pays (docs/RANKING.md §6 and §10, the middle-management plan's P5), per department whose delegation is not off (company/departments.json): its delegated items (an item with a delegated child run, or worked by piece lanes of a recorded split) against its single-seat items of the same class, by the cost per accepted item (score.cost over the one-shot sum; a child run's cost is its lead's family's, lib/family.js). keep when the delegated cost per accepted item is lower, withdraw when it is not over at least minItems delegated items (the dispatcher then withdraws the department's splitting once per evaluation; only the owner resumes), not enough data below minItems or with no single-seat item of the same class to compare. Delete this section to switch the report off
_readBounds: every input is read from its end, inside these bounds (docs/RETENTION.md)
